blocking: The language FAQ never clearly answers whether a parent can speak directly with the planner in their preferred language; translated pages and spoken support are blurred together.
The contingency section promises precise timing and an unchanged plan without explaining how delays, venue changes or substitute staff are actually handled.

fixes.where: how-we-work.html — language FAQ and 'A page for the parents'
fixes.what: Separate English planning, written translation and spoken support. Say: 'Tell us which language your family needs for calls and meetings. Before booking, we confirm who will provide that support, its availability and any additional fee.'
fixes.why: Parents need to know who can actually understand them before they commit.

fixes.what: Replace repeated 'timeline is re-called' and 'the plan does not change' with concrete procedures: agree priorities and spending approvals, revise timing with the officiant and venue, notify family contacts, and hand the current plan to the named backup.
fixes.why: Operational specifics earn more trust than assurances that disruption changes nothing.

fixes.what: Add a compact 'Find your celebration' list linking to each panel; retain the existing inquiry CTA after the panels.
fixes.why: On phones, six stacked panels make families scroll through unrelated ceremonies to find their own.

fixes.what: Replace the fixed 'one night … the next' sequence with: 'Henna, blessings, music and dancing, across the gatherings your family chooses. We agree the timing and participants with you.'
fixes.why: The prominent introduction should reflect the flexibility already promised in the supporting copy.

fixes.where: index.html and how-we-work.html — Full planning service descriptions
fixes.what: Change 'Begins at the first conversation' to 'Planning begins once your proposal is signed and deposit received'; describe the first conversation separately as discussing fit, scope and fees.
fixes.why: The current wording conflicts with the booking explanation and can imply planning work begins before engagement.
